svg.title: TrustRAG defense in the PoisonedRAG pipeline
svg.desc: Left to right: query and poisoned knowledge base feed the retriever, which returns a top-5 holding on average 4.65 poison and 0.35 clean passages. TrustRAG stage 1 re-embeds the top-k with SimCSE, gates on ROUGE-L overlap above 0.25, clusters with K-means (k = 2) and drops clusters whose mean cosine exceeds 0.88, cutting poison reaching the LLM from 4.65 to 0.09 per question. Stage 2 makes three calls to the target LLM (internal knowledge, consolidation, final answer). Robust attack success falls from 0.85 to 0.09; Vicuna-7B loses 0.07 clean accuracy. Caveat: the filter works because the five poison texts per question are near-duplicates.

g.text: usual: both clusters dense → drop all
Adaptive-attacker caveat. Stage 1 fires only because the 5 poison texts per
question are near-duplicates: all 1,000 poison pairs exceed ROUGE-L 0.25
(median 0.49, min 0.28), and the poison-pair cosine p10 (0.88) sits exactly at the
threshold. Diverse, non-duplicate poison was not tested and would likely pass.
Read as “defeats the published PoisonedRAG texts”, not as a general defense.
Figure 1. TrustRAG as deployed in our PoisonedRAG pipeline (BEIR NQ, full 100-question protocol, top-k = 5, N = 5 poison texts per question; means over 3 retrieval setups × 3 LLMs): Stage 1 removes
the near-duplicate poison cluster (4.65 → 0.09 poison passages per question) and Stage 2 reconciles what remains with the LLM’s own knowledge, cutting robust ASR from 0.85 to 0.09; only Vicuna-7B

† Robust ASR = exact match for Vicuna-7B, answered-only for Qwen3.5-27B, typography-normalized for gpt-oss-120b (per LLM 0.85 → 0.09, 0.90 → 0.08, 0.79 → 0.09). * Contriever cells use upstream’s precomputed BEIR
top-100 instead of FAISS (same top-k on 100/100 questions). Sources: experiments/RESULTS.md Step 5 (Tables D1–D3) and experiments/defenses/trustrag_filter_simcse_*.json.
